chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Abi Baseer, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who divorces his wife before consummating the marriage, so he said: 'She is irrevocably separated from him, and she may marry whomever she wishes from that very moment.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorce before consummation in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that in the absence of consummation (dakhul), the divorce is immediate and the wife is free to remarry without observing the standard three-month waiting period (iddah), a ruling derived from the principle that the primary purpose of iddah is to ascertain paternity. This specific interpretation is central to Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from some Sunni schools that may require a shorter, single menstrual cycle or one period. The narration underscores the practical implication that the marital bond is effectively severed at the moment of pronouncement when no cohabitation has occurred.
